definition: Localizing actions in video using only video-level labels rather than temporal annotations, typically via attention or multiple-instance learning.
details: Localizing actions in video using only video-level labels rather than temporal annotations, typically via attention or multiple-instance learning.

explainer.lead: Weakly supervised action localization finds actions in video using only video-level labels rather than temporal annotations. It matters because it avoids the cost of marking exact timestamps.

tiers.eli5: You are told a video contains someone cooking, but not which seconds, and the system has to find the cooking moments itself.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers typically use attention or multiple-instance learning to locate actions from video-level labels. The pitfall is weaker temporal precision than full temporal annotation.
tiers.paperLevel: Localizing actions in video using only video-level labels rather than temporal annotations, typically via attention or multiple-instance learning.

explainer.example: Given a video labeled "cooking" at the video level, the model highlights the segments where cooking occurs.
